issues.required_change:
In §10.2 add `crisis: { looks: CrisisLookRow[]; settings: CrisisLookSettings } /* item 122: a look only, below (*Crisis looks*) */` to `RosterTables`. Declare `interface CrisisLookRow { kind: 'siege'|'blockade'|'refugeeCamp'|'quarantine'|'famine'|'beast'|'raiders'|'disaster'|'occupation'|'rebellion'|'boom'|'bust' /* the look kinds of item 122 (b); §7.7's derivation row maps every SettlementForge stressor type and condition archetype to one kind or 'none' */; place: 'beyondWalls'|'approachRoads'|'approachByGate'|'outside'|'affectedQuarter'|'fields'|'edge'|'outlyingFarms'|'gatesAndKeep'|'streets'|'neighbourhoods'; band: 'city'|'district'|'neighbourhood' /* the coarsest band it shows at (item 122 (d)) */; scale: Record<Rung, [number, number]> /* its extent at severity 0 and 1, linear between: a hamlet a war band's camp, a city a full siege line */; priority: number /* the outskirts' order: siege, then quarantine, then refugees */ }` and `interface CrisisLookSettings { densityCap: number /* the share of the outskirts' free land the crisis looks may take together */; siegeStandoffM: number /* ≈ 300, beyond bowshot */ }` (values V11's look, symbol, scale and placement tables). Add a bullet *Crisis looks (item 122; J135)* stating:
(a) A look only. The table is read by §8.2's crisis look rows, §11's picture exports, the battle-map image and Find's listing, never by a stage, so no crisis changes the model or its hash. A look is drawn from the `ConditionOverlay`s standing in the view's week (§2.7, §2.9's `yearWeek`), and the aftermath reaches the map only through the epoch path (V06).
(b) Every stressor type and archetype has a row or 'none'; the regional_* pressures are 'none'.
(c) Placement is by keyed draws from the seed, the condition's id and the place (item 118 (e)'s keying). Scale follows severity and tier. Several crises share the outskirts by `priority` under `densityCap`. Nothing is placed on water, a gate's passage or a label's keep-out.
(d) A siege's camps stand `siegeStandoffM` beyond the walls, with its line of trenches round the town and its engines facing the gates or the weakest stretch (item 114's condition); an unwalled place gets blockade camps on its approach roads.
(e) A refugee camp stands on common or fallow land along the main approach road by a gate, where V06's growth frontier would build.
(f) Famine overrides item 117's crop stage.
(g) A disaster ruins whole neighbourhoods by a share of its severity: fire downwind through contiguous blocks, flood the low ground by the water, earthquake scattered. The calamity's `targets` win where the dossier names the place hit.
(h) Item 122 (h), J138: where the dossier gives a force's or a group's size, the look is sized by headcount, never by severity guesswork. `CrisisLookSettings` gains `areaPerHeadM2: number /* 45: each army's camp area per head; a travelling group's camp (migrants, pilgrims, a caravan) at the same rate */` and `enginesPerBesiegers: number /* 1 500: about one siege engine per this many besiegers, capped by the gates and wall stretches they can face */`. Two armies joined make twice the camped ground. A coalition's armies each keep their own camp and colours, spread round the town, the larger the coalition the fuller the ring. Where no size is given, (b)'s scale by severity and tier holds, with the calamity's or condition's own counts (`exodus`, arrivals) where it has them. Camps stay on the land the map holds; a force too large for the frame and its margin fills it out to the margin, the rest drawn by §8.8's massed marks.
Name §13.2's item-122 rows as its bars.

issues.claim: The closed-arc rules repair r1 added (VEW-03) contradict the wall grading. §4.2 S3 (4) counts 'a cliff, a gorge, a marsh, a sheer face, a river's banks round a loop' as closing arcs and allows picks only on approachable arcs. S3 (9) says 'Every arc closed (a mesa town; …): the stage walls nothing — no Enceinte is recorded for it and it has no gate', and §4.4 S5a step 1 says 'a stage whose every arc closes walls nothing and records no enceinte'. But §4.4 S5a step 1 itself says 'a steep slope or marsh closes behind a light wall', §4.8 *Graded by stretch* lays 'a lighter parapet on cliff tops, steep slopes and waterfronts', and V11 §3.16.1's rows give `cliff` 'closes: yes, wall: parapet' and `steepSlope`/`marsh` 'closes: yes, wall: light'. Only `sheerCliff`, `deepWater` and `gorge` close with no wall. So a mesa ringed by `cliff`-class arcs (≥ 60 % over ≥ 6 m, below the sheer test), or a marsh-ringed town, is walled by §4.8 and V11 but unwalled with no Enceinte by S3 (9). If walled, it has no gate, because no pick may fall on a closing arc: an undefined outcome either way.
issues.required_change: In §4.2 S3 (9) and §4.4 S5a step 1, make 'every arc closed' mean every arc whose defensibility row (V11 §3.16.1) has wall `none` (`sheerCliff`, `deepWater`, `gorge`); for those, keep the text ('walls nothing … no Enceinte … no gate'). Add, in (9): 'Where every arc closes but some carry a parapet or light wall (the `cliff`, `steepSlope` or `marsh` rows), the stage is walled on those arcs by §4.8's grade and records its Enceinte. It takes N₁ = 1 gate, picked on its walled closing arcs, least defensible first (`steepSlope`, then `marsh`, then `cliff`; then the pick contour's order), its route reaching it within §4.3's class grade limit, else by F-ROUTE's ladder. Reported (`W_WALLED_BY_BARRIERS`).' In (4), state which arcs are approachable: those whose row does not close, plus a sea or lake shore as (4) already counts it. Add a mesa below the sheer test and a marsh-ringed town to EP-21's fixtures.
